```sql

FROM your_table_name;
```

## 2. Using GROUP BY (More flexible)

```sql
SELECT column1, column2, column3
FROM your_table_name
GROUP BY column1, column2, column3;
```

```sql
SELECT column1, column2, column3
FROM (
    SELECT column1, column2, column3,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY column1, column2 ORDER BY column3) as rn
    FROM your_table_name
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1;
```

This keeps only the first occurrence of each group (based on the ORDER BY clause).

If you have a table with duplicate customer orders:

```sql
-- Using DISTINCT

FROM orders;

GROUP BY customer_id, order_date, product_name;
```
